newsitem.title: USA: Digital, Fritz Cos settle federal suit.
newsitem.headline: Digital, Fritz Cos settle federal suit.

text.p: U.S. Attorney Donald Stern said on Wednesday that Digital Equipment Corp and Fritz Cos agreed to pay $240,000 to settle the government's civil charges that they did not use U.S.-flagged air carriers to ship equipment overseas under a foreign-aid program.
Stern said that in reaching the settlement, Digital and Fritz expressly denied the government's allegations.

Under the Fly America Act, federal contractors must use U.S.-flag carriers when available. Stern said Digital shipped $6 million in computers and equipment to Pakistan under arrangements made by Fritz, using mostly non-U.S.-flag carriers.
Stern said Digital and Fritz certified that no U.S.-flag carrier was available, based on the size of the shipments. A government investigation alleged that U.S.-flag carriers were in fact available.
Transportation costs for such foreign aid shipments are passed on to the government. Stern termed the $240,000 payment a "recovery."
